newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Philippine President Fidel Ramos was admitted to the Makati Medical Centre for a series of medical tests. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The group advocating a change in the Constitution vows to step up its efforts to organise more groups in pushing for the extension of the term of President Ramos. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Congress will try to break the impasse that has prevented the two chambers from passing the proposed 1997 national budget at a two-day special session called by President Ramos (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Time magazine's 1996 Man of the Year is AIDS research scientist Dr. David Ho, who pioneered a treatment for HIV infection that has shown promise in beating back the deadly disease (INQUIRER)

- Hong Kong-based Hottick Investment Ltd has agreed to increase its newly acquired equity in National Steel Corp from 70 to 82.50 percent after the completion of a buy-out agreement with Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd of Malaysia, NSC chief executive officer Edgardo Espiritur says. (BUSINESS DAILY)

- The heavy influx of workers' remittances and regular Central Bank intervention in the foreign exchange market pushes the country's gross international reserves to $11.8 billion as of December 20, Central Bank treasury head Sergio Edeza says. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The Philippine economy expects to end the year with a bang with the Gross National Product projected to grow by more than 7.1 percent in the fourth quarter. (MANILA TIMES)
